next_steps: Run token/sec benchmark on dev model w/ sample dataset (Redwood to provision test harness)
Share dedicated vs hosted cost estimate spreadsheet
action_items: Ethan: Share cost spreadsheet and pilot playbook by 2026-11-02
Priya: Prepare benchmark harness and example load script by 2026-11-04
Nora: Provide sample traffic profile and max concurrency by 2026-11-01
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Martin (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (BridgePoint CTO), Rafael Gomez (BridgePoint ML Eng), Nora Patel (Infra Lead), Samir Rao (Security)
summary: Initial technical discovery to determine whether BridgePoint should use Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private for a conversational agent with strict p95 latency and burst token throughput requirements. Main asks: p95 < 200ms for short responses, predictable concurrency of 120 active streams, and token/sec profiling for both streaming and non-streaming loads. Security/FFI: SOC2, KMS, and VPC integration are blockers for private deployment timeline.
topics: security controls: KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, um, this is Ethan from Redwood, I'm the AE working with BridgePoint, with Priya and Liam from our solutions team. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya: Good, hi, thanks. We're excited to get into the numbers.
[00:18] Rafael: Yeah, we have a pretty tight p95 target and some pretty spiky traffic patterns.
[00:25] Priya: Quick agenda — we'll align on goals, probe current infra, then dig into latency and token throughput expectations and tooling to run the benchmarks. Sound good?
[00:34] Nora: Yup. Also security requirements; Samir will handle that part.
[00:38] Samir: Quick note, SOC2 plus customer-driven audit logs, and all keys in our KMS, that is non-negotiable.
[00:45] Ethan: Understood. Can you share the p95 numbers you're projecting?
[00:50] Maya: We're aiming for p95 generation latency under 200ms for short responses — say 20 tokens — and for streaming endpoints we want p95 chunk latency under 120ms.
[01:02] Rafael: On concurrency, we're planning for 120 concurrent active sessions during business hours, but bursts up to 400 for 30-90s during campaigns.
[01:12] Priya: OK, good. A couple clarifying q's: are those p95 numbers measured end-to-end from the client or just server-side inference?
[01:20] Nora: End-to-end, front-end to response for the user perceived latency. That includes network and SDK overhead.
[01:27] Priya: That's helpful — so we'll need to account for edge latency and routing. For hosted vs dedicated, that influences routing decisions, region pinning, and network egress.
[01:36] Liam: Also worth thinking about warm vs cold KV cache for long chats; cold starts can add variance.
[01:44] Rafael: Right, we have a lot of short dialogs, but some longer threads where KV grows.
[01:49] Ethan: Quick note on measurement methodology: we recommend synthetic load tests that mimic your client-side stack — same SDKs, same chunk sizing for streaming — and capture p95 at both client (browser/mobile) and server (inference host). We'll supply a harness.
[02:05] Maya: Good — can you run a token/sec benchmark with our dev model? We have a 7B dense model fine-tuned for QA.
[02:13] Priya: Absolutely. We'll need a sample prompt set and the model artifact or a containerized runtime. We can run both streaming and non-streaming passes to show token/sec and p95 distributions.
[02:26] Rafael: For the dev run, what hardware will you use and how comparable is that to hosted?
[02:31] Priya: We'll run on Redwood-simulated stack that matches our dedicated tier — A100 equivalent nodes with quantization-friendly paths; for hosted, the multi-tenant profile is slightly different but we'll include both data points.
[02:43] Samir: Security question: if you run a benchmark on our dataset, how's data handled? We need logs scrubbed and any artifacts retained only per our retention policy.
[02:52] Ethan: We can run it inside a short-lived sandbox, and provide options to run the harness inside your VPC — that would remove data egress concerns. We'll send the protocol for scrub/retention.
[03:02] Nora: Timeline: we need an internal decision by mid-November. Ideally pilot starts week of Nov 8. Can you support that?
[03:09] Ethan: Yes, that's feasible. We'll aim to have the benchmark and cost estimate by Nov 4 so you can review.
[03:16] Priya: Let's get into the specifics — tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated for your p95. Hosted: fastest onboarding and lower ops but less control over reserved capacity; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and capacity to meet p95 under burst. Private (VPC) adds network isolation but takes longer and needs on-prem or private cloud setup.
[03:34] Rafael: If we choose hosted, how do you guarantee p95 during bursts?
[03:38] Liam: We use smart routing and auto-burst pools; but for hard SLOs we usually recommend dedicated so you have reserved GPU pools with an SLA. For hosted, we can set capacity alarms and fallback to a smaller model variant if load spikes.
[03:51] Rafael: Fallback to smaller model — does that mean quality is different mid-flight?
[03:55] Priya: Potentially, yes. We can configure automatic rollbacks or structured responses that indicate a degraded result. You can also pin critical routes to Dedicated to avoid that.
[04:05] Maya: For streaming chunk sizes, what chunk length yields the best token/sec vs latency tradeoff?
[04:11] Priya: Typically 16-32 token chunks for low p95 at the cost of more frequent network round-trips. If you batch at the edge you can lower per-token cost but increase chunk latency. We'll show both profiles in the benchmark.
[04:23] Rafael: Is there support for per-customer KV cache to improve long-thread latency?
[04:27] Liam: Yes, we support KV caching and prefix caching. Per-customer KV is available on Dedicated and Private for isolation; on Hosted it's multi-tenant but we provide strong isolation guarantees and TTLs.
[04:38] Samir: Encryption at rest/in transit — we require CMEK integration with our AWS KMS and full audit logs. Can Redwood do per-tenant CMEK?
[04:47] Ethan: Yes, across Dedicated and Private. Hosted also supports customer keys via KMS in specific tiers but Private gives you full control. We'll include the KMS integration doc.
[04:56] Nora: Network topology — we need to avoid extra egress hops. If we choose Dedicated in our region, can we peer VPC and keep traffic internal?
[05:03] Priya: Yes, Dedicated and Private both support VPC peering and private endpoints. Hosted can also be region pinned but may traverse our managed edges — we'll show latency delta in the benchmark.
[05:14] Rafael: On concurrency: 120 steady active sessions, 400 bursts. How do you size GPU pools?
[05:19] Liam: Depends on model throughput; for 7B quantized we might see 20-40 tokens/sec per GPU for generation workloads under streaming. For your concurrency, we'd size a pool to handle steady-state plus headroom and configure autoscale for bursts with a cold/warm buffer. We'll provide a capacity plan after we run token/sec profiling.
[05:39] Maya: I'd like a clear p95 accounting: what percent is network, what percent is inference, and what part is SDK overhead.
[05:46] Priya: Agreed — our report will break down p95 into client-side, edge, routing, and inference. We'll instrument each hop and provide traces.
[05:55] Rafael: Can Redwood run an in-situ benchmark inside our VPC to avoid network noise?
[05:59] Ethan: Yes, we can run the harness in your VPC (Private pilot) or run a Hosted benchmark from your region to simulate real e2e. Both are options — the VPC in-situ run reduces variance.
[06:10] Samir: We also need to evaluate failure modes — what happens when cache is cold during a burst?
[06:14] Liam: Cold cache increases token generation work; we'll simulate cold-start scenarios and show p95 delta. Also, we can enable prefix caching to mitigate.
[06:21] Maya: For the pilot, we want three scenarios: steady-state streaming at 120 concurrent; a 90s 400-concurrency burst; and mixed long-thread scenarios to stress KV.
[06:32] Priya: Perfect — we'll design scripts for those three. Please upload representative prompts and dataset to the sandbox link we'll share.
[06:40] Rafael: Pricing — how does dedicated pricing look vs hosted per-token for heavy streaming?
[06:45] Ethan: We'll send a detailed cost model. Short answer: Dedicated reduces per-token unit cost at the expense of commit; hosted is pay-as-you-go and can be cheaper if bursts are infrequent. We'll include a break-even analysis.
[06:58] Nora: What about model quantization — do you support int8 / nf4 and will that change latency numbers?
[07:03] Priya: Yes, we support several quantization profiles. Int8/NF4 typically reduces memory and improves throughput but can slightly affect quality. We'll include quantized vs full precision profiles in the benchmark.
[07:15] Rafael: Any concerns about streaming consistency under autoscale?
[07:18] Liam: With continuous batching and KV cache affinity, we maintain consistent latency; autoscale can introduce node warm-up time. We mitigate by maintaining a small warm buffer in Dedicated or using burst pools.
[07:29] Maya: Can you do canary rollouts for new model versions without impacting the SLAs?
[07:33] Ethan: Yes, our rollout system supports canary percentages and automatic rollback on quality regressions. That said, canaries still use capacity, so plan for it in the pool sizing.
[07:42] Samir: Auditability — we need request-level logs for 90 days and immutable audit trails for admin actions.
[07:49] Ethan: Redwood Console supports that as an addon; we'll note retention and immutability options in the compliance pack.
[07:56] Rafael: Ok, two quick technical nitty-gritty items: tokenization differences between our tokenizer and your serving stack — could that skew token/sec?
[08:03] Priya: It could. We'll run the benchmark using your tokenizer to keep token accounting consistent. If necessary, bring a containerized tokenizer step in the harness.
[08:12] Maya: Also WAN jitter — can you re-run the streaming test with simulated jitter to see p95 impact?
[08:18] Liam: Absolutely. We'll include jitter/noise profiles to show sensitivity.
[08:22] Ethan: Next steps recap — Priya and Liam to run token/sec and p95 benchmarks (streaming and non-streaming) in two environments: Redwood Dedicated-sim node and inside BridgePoint VPC if you choose. Ethan will share cost spreadsheet and SOC2 + KMS docs. Pilot kickoff week of Nov 8 is target.
[08:40] Nora: One more timeline constraint: our infra team can only dedicate time on Nov 2-5 to onboard the pilot. Can you hit that?
[08:46] Priya: We'll accelerate. We'll provide the harness and a short onboarding runbook so your team can set up quickly.
[08:52] Rafael: For the benchmark, please include percentile histograms, not just p95 and p99.
[08:58] Priya: Will do.
[09:01] Maya: Any red flags you see for us choosing Dedicated vs Hosted today?
[09:07] Ethan: Given your strict p95 and high bursts, Dedicated is safer for SLOs. Hosted could work if you accept fallback model variants and slightly higher variance. Since you require KMS and VPC peering, Dedicated or Private seems likely. But the benchmark will give the decision evidence.
[09:23] Samir: Ok. Please include a matrix of pros/cons including compliance and time-to-live for Private.
[09:29] Ethan: We'll include that. Anything else?
[09:33] Maya: No, that's it. Thanks.
[09:35] Ethan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts and the proposed pilot schedule.
[09:40] (call ends, ~52 minutes total)

Notes: occasional transcription glitches — e.g., "KV" rendered as "kayvee" in places, speaker labels auto-attributed in two spots. Shared artifacts referenced: cost spreadsheet (link to be sent), security pack https://redwood.ai/security/bridgepoint-snapshot.pdf, benchmark harness repo https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/tree/bridgepoint
end_notes: Call ended with clear pilot plan and benchmarks requested. Redwood team to provide cost model, SOC2/KMS docs, and run three benchmark scenarios (steady, burst, long-thread). BridgePoint to provide prompt sets and traffic profile. Target pilot week: 2026-11-08.
